raw: {"need": "Competence", "secondary": {"name": "Status"}, "read": "One visible mistake in front of a customer landed hard on their sense of whether they are actually good at this job. The triple-checking is not conscientiousness; it is a nervous system trying to guarantee it never gets exposed like that again. The slowdown is the cost of running on fear instead of confidence, and underneath it is a real question: do I still belong here after this.", "pull": {"collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Back off, stop assigning anything high-stakes, and let the over-checking continue unchallenged to avoid adding pressure, which quietly tells them the mistake proved they cannot handle it."}, "mentorMove": "Name the mistake once, close it out cleanly, and then treat them as someone whose job is to ship work at pace, not to be perfect in slow motion. Hold the velocity standard while giving them a way to rebuild trust that does not require flawless output.", "holdFirm": ["Work still goes out on the agreed timeline.", "One round of checking is the standard, not an open-ended loop."], "stayFlexible": ["A short window where they flag anything uncertain to you before it ships, so there is a safety net that does not crater pace.", "How you two define a reasonable spot-check so they have a concrete process rather than free-floating anxiety."], "forceLevel": {"level": 3, "label": "Collaboration"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "I want to talk about what has happened since that customer issue, and I want to start by being straight with you: mistakes that reach a customer are not nothing, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. But what I am watching you do right now is not the fix."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Tell me what is going through your head when you are checking the same thing four times. What are you actually afraid of catching, or not catching?"}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I want to build with you. A quick, defined check process you actually trust, so you can run it once and move. And for the next couple of weeks, if something feels genuinely risky, flag it to me before it goes out. Not forever, just long enough for you to get your footing back."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "I need you shipping at the pace this role requires, and I am holding you to that because I have watched your work and I know you are capable of it. One mistake does not change my read on you. Grinding to a halt does not protect you; it just means the customer issue costs us twice."}], "longGame": "The real skill here is learning to work with a calibrated process rather than with anxiety as the quality control. situation: A junior shipped something with a mistake a customer caught, and now they are triple-checking everything and velocity has cratered.
